playoff_odds.how: 10,000 simulated seasons: each remaining game's score is drawn from that team's own weekly scores (with under 4 weeks, every team's scores shifted to its mean), and teams are seeded by wins, then total points, as the league's settings say.

record_vs_median.how: Each week my score against the median of every team's score that week, beside all-play (my score against every other team's each week).

lineup_efficiency.how: Each week the best lineup my roster allowed under the league's slot rules, with hindsight, minus what I started; ranked against every team (1 = fewest points left on the bench); and, apart, waiver adds that out-produced their baseline but sat on my bench.

start_sit.how: A close call is a starter and the best-projected bench player who could fill that slot projected within 3 points of each other; it was right if the starter scored at least as much.

consistency.how: Standard deviation of my weekly scores divided by their mean (lower = steadier), ranked against every team (1 = steadiest).

strength_of_schedule.how: The season scoring average of each opponent I've played, averaged, minus the league's average weekly score; ranked against every team (1 = hardest schedule).

draft_value.how: For each of my picks, its rank in points per game among every drafted player who has played, minus where it was drafted (negative = better than its draft slot).

waiver_impact.how: Points scored in my starting lineup by players I didn't draft (waivers, free agents, trades), and their share of my starters' points.

position_share.how: Share of my starters' points from each position, beside the average of every team's shares.

schedule_what_if.how: My scores replayed against each other team's opponents week by week (where that opponent was me, against that team instead); how many of those schedules give me a better or worse record.

margins.how: My score minus my opponent's each completed week; close games are decided by under 5 points.

waiver_adds.how: Each add after the draft, judged on all his points while on my roster (started or benched) against the dropped player's per game on another team over the same weeks, or the positional replacement level; then a hit captured (out-produced and started at least half his weeks), a hit left on the bench, a miss, a stash (still rostered, under 2 weeks or on injured reserve) or insurance (a handcuff to my own starter, never started). Hit rate (both kinds of hit over hits and misses) with a 95% Wilson interval. Available is his net points over the baseline across every week he was on my roster; captured is the same net over only the weeks I started him, so captured can exceed available when his benched weeks were below the baseline. Every add is listed, with the best and worst three by available flagged.

draft.how: Each of my picks' points to date against the median points to date of every player taken in that round, league-wide.

quadrant.how: For every team in my leagues, the all-play win share (wins against every other team each week) against actual wins minus all-play wins; my teams carry their week-by-week trail. Other teams are points only, never named.

draft.how: Points per week my drafted starters scored above the median player taken in the same round, league-wide, over the season so far; rank and percentile among every manager across my leagues.

lineup.how: Points per week my chosen lineup lost against the best possible lineup from my roster, the league's median manager as zero; rank and percentile across my leagues.

moves.how: Points per week from players I added, dropped or traded against keeping my drafted roster; rank and percentile across my leagues.

strength.how: My all-play win share over the completed weeks, pooled across my teams, with a Wilson interval; rank in each league and, for the percentile, among every manager across my leagues.

composite.how: The four components standardised and averaged, as the share of managers across my leagues I beat, with a bootstrap interval over weeks.

album_half_life.how: For albums with at least 10 plays in their first 7 days, an exponential decay fitted (Poisson, by maximum likelihood) to daily plays over their first 8 weeks; the median half-life across albums, and this week's most-played album with its half-life so far.

discovery.how: Share of each month's plays by artists first played that month (none earlier in the archive); months with at least 50 plays, from the archive's second month.

album_listener.how: Share of plays whose previous play, within 15 minutes, is the preceding track of the same album.
album_listener.missing: track number on the album (scrobbles carry the album's name only)

concentration.how: Each month (with at least 50 plays) the five most-played artists' share of plays; and the most plays of one track in one day.

heatmap.how: Plays by weekday (Monday first) and hour, Pacific; and plays per weekday against per weekend day, over every day since the first play.

genre_mix.how: Each month's plays (months with at least 50) by the artist's top Last.fm tag, the 8 largest named, the rest as other; artists not yet looked up are untagged.

comebacks.how: Artists with at least 20 plays in a month after 3 or more months with none (and some play before that), newest first.

first_repeat.how: Hours between a new track's first and second play (new = first played after the archive's first 30 days); the median over tracks played twice.

entropy.how: Shannon entropy, in bits, of the month's plays across artists, for months with at least 50 plays; higher means plays spread over more artists.

nostalgia.how: The median release year of the tracks played each month, for months with at least 50 plays.

enduring.how: From Apple Music's lifetime play counts: each artist's plays divided by the years since the first track of theirs was added to my library, for artists in the library at least a year.

retention_new_artists.how: For each month, the artists I played for the first time, and the share of them played again in the 30 and 90 days after that first play; months whose 90 days are not up yet are left out.

artist_survival.how: Kaplan–Meier curves of how long an artist stays in rotation (months from first play to the last one, with a play in the 60 days before the export counting as still in rotation), catalog against new, for artists first played since the 2023 Apple Music sync; a Cox hazard ratio of new against catalog, and per five years of gap between an artist's release years and the year I added them; the log-rank test. The export records no play before 2023-03-01 (its earliest last_played), so an end before that day is invisible.

values.cohort: Artists first played since the 2023 Apple Music sync; those already in the library before it are left out.

artist_survival_all.how: The same analysis with the artists already in the library before the 2023 sync included, their first play taken from the library's date added. The export records no play before 2023-03-01 (its earliest last_played), so an end before that day is invisible.

values.cohort: Every artist, including those in the library before the 2023 sync, dated from the library.

album_listening.how: For each album with at least 20 plays, the Gini coefficient of plays across its tracks (0: every track played alike, 1: one track only); the value is the share of albums under 0.4, the ones I play through.

discovery_direction.how: Of the tracks added to the library each year, the share released at least 5 years earlier (digging back) against the rest (keeping up), by the year added; tracks added on the sync date are left out.

volume_lag.how: Pearson correlation between a week's training volume (weight × reps over working sets) and the change in mean best e1RM the following week, with a Fisher interval.

consistency.how: Weeks grouped by sessions logged, with the mean change in best e1RM over the following week; the value is the correlation between the two.

hours_by_month.how: Hours watched each month by type, from dated watches with a known runtime (backfilled past watches count no hours); months with at least 5 hours.

show.how: Share of the shows I've watched (any status but plan to watch) carrying each Simkl genre, the 8 most common.

film.how: Share of the films I've watched (any status but plan to watch) carrying each Simkl genre, the 8 most common.

anime.how: Share of the animes I've watched (any status but plan to watch) carrying each Simkl genre, the 8 most common.

by_year.how: By the year I watched them (dated watches only), the share of titles carrying each genre; years with at least 1 titles.

release_decades.how: Films I've finished by the decade they came out.

show.how: Finished over finished plus dropped; titles on hold are counted separately, in neither.

film.how: Finished over finished plus dropped; titles on hold are counted separately, in neither.

anime.how: Finished over finished plus dropped; titles on hold are counted separately, in neither.

pace.how: For finished shows and anime with dated episode logs (never backfilled ones), weeks from the first to the last logged episode against the episodes logged; the median pace in episodes a week.

show.how: Share of the shows I've watched by Simkl's country of origin; titles whose Simkl country is known to be wrong are left out and noted.

film.how: Share of the films I've watched by Simkl's country of origin; titles whose Simkl country is known to be wrong are left out and noted.

anime.how: Share of the animes I've watched by Simkl's country of origin; titles whose Simkl country is known to be wrong are left out and noted.

excluded: Title 2: Simkl gives the wrong country

films.how: For my top ten, Simkl's community rating; the Spearman rank correlation between my order and theirs (95% interval by Fisher's z), and the title placed furthest above and below where the community would put it among those ten.

shows.how: For my top ten, Simkl's community rating; the Spearman rank correlation between my order and theirs (95% interval by Fisher's z), and the title placed furthest above and below where the community would put it among those ten.

anime.how: For my top ten, Simkl's community rating; the Spearman rank correlation between my order and theirs (95% interval by Fisher's z), and the title placed furthest above and below where the community would put it among those ten.

runtime.how: Runtime of the films I've finished: the median, and the share over 120 minutes.

backlog.how: From the date each title went on my plan-to-watch list, the median days until its first dated watch (from 5 started titles); and titles added to that list against titles finished, each month (backfilled titles left out).

values.first_unit: one title finished with both a start and an end date

first_episode_drops.how: Shows and anime I dropped with at most one episode watched, over every show and anime I started; titles backfilled with no episodes logged are left out (how far I got isn't known).

keeping_up.how: For shows and anime I'm watching that are still airing, episodes watched against episodes released (titles backfilled with no episodes logged are left out).

films.how: How my tiered (finished) titles split across tiers S to D.

shows.how: How my tiered (finished) titles split across tiers S to D.

anime.how: How my tiered (finished) titles split across tiers S to D.

tier_genres_decades.how: For each tier with at least 5 titles (films, shows and anime together), the share carrying each Simkl genre (the 5 most common) and the share from each release decade.

films.how: Over every tiered title, the Spearman rank correlation between my tier and Simkl's community rating (95% interval by Fisher's z), and the titles whose tier sits furthest above and below their rating, comparing percentile ranks within the type.

shows.how: Over every tiered title, the Spearman rank correlation between my tier and Simkl's community rating (95% interval by Fisher's z), and the titles whose tier sits furthest above and below their rating, comparing percentile ranks within the type.

anime.how: Over every tiered title, the Spearman rank correlation between my tier and Simkl's community rating (95% interval by Fisher's z), and the titles whose tier sits furthest above and below their rating, comparing percentile ranks within the type.

tier_completion_pace.how: For each tier, completion (finished over finished plus dropped; tiers cover finished titles, so this falls below 1 only if a tiered title is later dropped) and, for shows and anime with at least 3 dated titles in the tier, the median pace in episodes a week (backfilled watches never count).

s_tier.how: The share of tiered titles in S, by type and by release decade; and for each genre carried by at least 10 titles, its share among S titles divided by its share among B titles.

tier_model.how: An ordered logistic model of my tier from Simkl's community score, release year, runtime and the top genres, scored by leave-one-out accuracy against always guessing the commonest tier.

taste_drift.how: Mean tier score (S=4, A=3, B=2, C=1, D=0) of the titles I finished each year, from the year each was first watched; the value is a straight line's slope per year.

community_gap_by_genre.how: For each genre carried by at least 15 titles, my mean tier score minus the tier score Simkl's community rating implies (its rating mapped to tiers by my own quantiles), with a 95% interval.

pace_vs_tier.how: Mean tier score of finished titles with dated episodes, by pace: binge (3 or more episodes a week), steady (1 to 3) and slow (under 1).

by_director.how: For each director with at least 3 of my finished films (TMDB credits), the mean of my tiers (S=4 to D=0), best first.

by_studio.how: For each studio with at least 3 of my finished anime (TMDB credits), the mean of my tiers, best first.

by_lead.how: For each lead actor (first billed on TMDB) with at least 3 of my finished films, the mean of my tiers, best first.

blockbuster.how: My finished films split into quartiles of TMDB popularity; the mean tier in each, and a straight line's slope across the quartiles with a 95% interval.

sequels.how: For each TMDB collection where I finished the first film and at least one later one, the later films' mean tier minus the first's; the value is the mean change.

language.how: My finished films by original language (TMDB): the share not in English, and the mean tier of each group.

critics_vs_audience.how: Films where the Rotten Tomatoes critic and audience scores (OMDb) differ by 20 points or more: whether my tier sides with the critics or the audience; the value is the critics' share with a Wilson interval.

crowd_agreement.how: Every tiered title's Simkl community score against my tier (S=4 to D=0): Spearman's rank correlation; the six largest gaps; the genres where my tiers run furthest above and below the community; and how often a tier predicted from the score alone is right, leave-one-out, against always guessing the commonest tier.

taste_profile.how: An ordered logistic model of my tier (S = 5 to D = 1) on each genre's presence and the standardised runtime and release year, over every tiered title; each effect with a 95% interval, clear when the interval excludes zero; accuracy leave-one-out against always guessing the commonest tier; the six largest gaps against the community score.

scores.how: Median and quartiles of my Beli scores, overall and by cuisine and by city (groups of at least 5 places).

choice_vs_taste.how: Each cuisine's share of the places I've tried against its share of my top quartile by score (cuisines with at least 5 places; the rest together as other).

order_effect.how: Score against the order places were ranked (1 = first), within cuisine (a fixed effect for each), as the change in score per 100 places with a 95% interval. Beli moves a place's ranked date when it's re-ranked.

contrast_effect.how: Score against the previous place's score (in the order ranked), within cuisine, as the slope with a 95% interval (positive: a good place before lifts the next one).

home_bias.how: Scores in my most-ranked city against everywhere else, within cuisine (a fixed effect for each), with a 95% interval; only cuisines tried both at home and away count.

contrarian.how: My scores against Beli's community score.
contrarian.missing: a community score (Beli's ranking response has none)

new_cuisines.how: Cuisines I ranked for the first time, counted by month (counts only, never which place); Beli moves a ranking's date when a place is re-ranked.

landing.how: The last 20 places I ranked for the first time and the percentile each sits at in my current ranking (1 = top, 0 = bottom); the value is their median; by month of first ranking when there are three months or more.

rerank_drift.how: For places I ranked more than once, the later score minus the first, grouped by time since the first ranking; the value is the mean change overall with a bootstrap interval.

safe_bet.how: For each cuisine with ten places or more, the middle half of my scores (first to third quartile) and the median; the narrowest middle half is the safest bet, the value.

lifting_soundtrack.how: Plays whose time falls between a workout's start and end: the most-played artists in workouts this month, and the artists played in sessions where a main lift's best e1RM was set.

plays.how: Plays by weekday (Monday first) and by hour, Pacific.

restaurants.how: Places ranked on Beli by weekday (Monday first), in the place's time zone; weekdays only, never a date.

time_budget.how: Hours by weekday over the last 8 weeks: watching from episode and film runtimes, listening from track lengths, training from workout durations.

win_chance.how: Every week's pre-game win chance against the result (a tie counts half), pooled over my teams: observed win rate per band of predicted chance, and the Brier score (mean squared error; 0.25 is what always saying 50% scores).

odds_over_time.how: My playoff odds as they stood before each week, against where I finished; published once the regular season is over.
